correctness.rationale: The tensor-product Lindblad generator yields a scalar damped oscillator with verified initial conditions and explicit repeated-root/overdamped solutions. Under the stated nearcritical scaling, alpha_n log n/(8k)->theta and delta_n log n->0; exact positive root gives u_n=0.5 log n+loglog n-log2+o(1), whence sqrt(n)z->g(theta)e^-c. For fixed p>4k, spectral separation gives sqrt(n)z->e^-c. The log-likelihood and bounded triangular-array CLT show TV->2Phi(a/2)-1, and channel contraction plus strict limiting profile yields epsilon-mixing centering. Executed the package verifier against actual finite-n binomial probabilities; no finite test is presented as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The mathematically natural mixing-time invariant is refined from an order estimate to full tolerance-dependent cutoff and a singular phase-boundary scaling. The defective-root factor produces a real n loglog n delay; perturbing decoherence on a (log n)^-2 scale yields a distinct universal sinh(theta)/theta transition. The result identifies exactly how fragile the critical mixing law is to n-dependent physical noise and supplies sharp asymptotics for quantum-walk sampling; this is not a numeric recomputation or arbitrary slice.
